question: Which implemented C9 decision best integrates HCI reasoning and demonstrated AI-agent direction/correction?
whyNewCriteria: Owner explicitly adds HCI and AI-agent best practices as joint priority; first round did not separately weight an actual agent-correction chain. Earlier verdict is challengeable, not input to fresh reviewers.

anchors: 3 research-grounded mechanism plus serious counterevidence and task limits
3 contemporaneous failure or discriminating comparison -> grounded correction/harness -> verified accepted behavior
3 one observable consequential behavior with credible alternatives
3 source plus scoped runtime/browser evidence, bounded claims

constraints: Do not read old verdicts into first fresh packets
No human preference or HD score inferred
Remote content safety is not same-object intention-preserving undo
Pending is bounded by actual command/draft/recovery behavior
A single C9 point, no umbrella list unless coherent one state boundary
steps: Build balanced fact packet from independent audits
Two no-history candidate reviews with reversed order
Run bounded discriminating technical or acceptance-oracle comparison if a material uncertainty remains
Fresh skeptical final review, refine and targeted recheck
Validate English files/citations/provenance, focused local commits
stop: One primary recommendation plus clearly subordinated context selected
Important source/code conflicts resolved or candidate downgraded
At least two substantive review/refinement steps, no rerun of resolved first-round lanes
Actual methods and unrun human work labeled
English round-2 evidence and main-index relationship clear
scope: Research/documentation. No runtime feature edits, deployment/provider calls, credential reads/changes or student reflection writing. Isolated local prototypes only if useful.
